newsitem.title: CHINA: China indices end down on new clampdown concern.
newsitem.headline: China indices end down on new clampdown concern.

text.p: China's A and B indices ended down on Thursday following widespread market talk of a looming market clampdown by securities authorities, brokers said.
Shenzhen's B share market was also badly hit by the 30 percent slump in profits reported by Great Ocean Shipping, which dived HK$0.33 or 7.62 percent to HK$4.00.
"There are not many B share companies," said an analyst at China Guotai Securities in Shenzhen. "If one posts poor results, investors get pessimistic about the rest."
Shanghai's B share index fell 0.41 points or 0.59 percent to 69.342 points on volume of 14.9 million shares worth $7.1 million against $7.6 million on Wednesday.
Shenzhen's B index lost 5.52 points or 3.29 percent to 162.14 points on thin turnover of HK$104.2 million compared with Wednesday's 109.7 million.
"We have heard a lot about a new clampdown on securities trading, which it is said will be announced by Beijing this weekend," a trader based in Shenzhen said.
Brokers on the Shanghai market said market sentiment was cautious amid uncertainty and poor company results, while the falls on the A share market compounded the declines.
Shanghai's A share index fell 43.385 points or 3.57 percent to 1,172.886 points on volume of 693.6 million shares worth 8.3 billion yuan, down from Wednesday's 9.3 billion yuan.
The SSE 30 blue-chip index tumbled 96.389 points or 2.98 percent to 3136.847 points.
"Two blue-chips recently posted lower-than-expected results and dividend plans, and this has also hurt market sentiment," said one broker.
In Shanghai, portable phone producer Eastern Communications was the biggest loser on both A and B share market due to a dividend plan which disappointed investors.

Its B share price slumped $0.068 or 6.75 percent to $0.938 on volume of one million shares and its A share price fell 2.71 yuan to its 10 percent daily limit-down of 24.38 yuan on volume of 1.2 million shares.
On Wednesday, the company posted 1996 net profits of 291.6 million yuan, up 14.3 percent from 255.2 million yuan in 1995.
It planned a cash dividend of 0.175 yuan per share for B share holders and a dividend of 0.048 yuan per share for A share holders from 1996 profits, a company statement said.
Shenzhen's A share index fell 9.96 points or 2.3 percent to end at 418.80 points on turnover of 9.6 billion yuan, compared with 10.3 billion yuan on Wednesday.
Computer hardware and software maker Shenzhen Kaifa Technology Co Ltd was the worst performer among the A shares, losing 2.77 yuan to 30.91 yuan as 3.4 million shares changed hands.
